title: [AUG-113] Live transcription with server-captured system audio (no picker in live mode)
why_we_need_this:
Follow-up to AUG-105 and AUG-112. Live transcription mode still forces the browser screen picker even when the user has System audio source = System, because the live pipeline (@client/src/services/liveTranscriptionClient.ts) taps browser MediaStreams with a ScriptProcessorNode and sends 4-second 16 kHz chunks over the WebSocket at /api/live-transcribe. A server-side capture (WASAPI helper, BlackHole, audiotee, dshow) produces a WAV on the server and no MediaStream in the browser, so the [Them] side of live mode has nothing to tap. FileUpload currently shows a notice and falls back to the picker for live recordings.

The server already owns the system audio in that case, so feeding it into the live pipeline server-side removes the picker from live mode entirely and avoids a second resampling hop in the browser.

Design:
1. Tee the capture stream on the server. In @server/src/services/systemCapture.ts the capture pipeline pipes helper/ffmpeg output into <captureId>.wav. Add an optional live sink: when a capture is started with { live: true } (POST /api/capture/start body), ffmpeg additionally writes 16 kHz mono s16le PCM to a second output on stdout (ffmpeg `-f s16le -ac 1 -ar 16000 pipe:1`, with the WAV file output kept as is via tee or two -map outputs). The server reads that PCM stream and pushes it into a ChunkAccumulator identical to the one used for WebSocket audio in @server/src/services/liveTranscription.ts, tagged speaker Them.
2. Bind the capture to a live session. Extend the WebSocket protocol in liveTranscription.ts with a small JSON control frame sent by the client right after connect: { type: 'attach-capture', captureId }. The server looks up the running capture, attaches its live sink to this connection's transcription loop (same engine setting: local whisper-cli or Groq), and rejects with a warning if the captureId is unknown or already attached.
3. Client: in @client/src/components/FileUpload.tsx remove the live-mode exclusion: when useServerCapture resolves to true and liveMode is on, start the capture with live: true, pass captureId to LiveTranscriptionClient.start(), and send only mic chunks over the WebSocket. LiveTranscriptionClient sends the attach-capture frame and stops creating the system ScriptProcessorNode when a captureId is present. Keep the browser path unchanged when the source resolves to browser.
4. Lifecycle: stopping the recording still calls POST /api/capture/stop; the server detaches the live sink first, flushes the last partial chunk through transcription, then finalizes the WAV so the post-recording dual-track transcript is produced exactly as today. If the WebSocket closes early the sink is detached but the capture keeps recording until /stop.
5. VAD and overlap: reuse the existing ChunkAccumulator (4 s windows, 1 s overlap, RMS gate 0.006) so live output quality is identical between browser-tapped and server-fed system audio.
6. Docs: project-context/transcription/live-transcription README documents the attach-capture frame, the server-fed Them source, and the detach/flush order; architecture README drops the "live mode uses the browser picker" statement.
acceptance_criteria:
- On this Windows PC with System audio source = System, starting a Live recording shows no screen picker and no "Live transcription uses the browser screen picker" notice; the live panel shows [Me] lines from the mic and [Them] lines from audio played through the headphones.
- The same recording, once stopped, still produces the post-recording dual-track transcript with [Me]/[Them] labels from the WAV files (live and post-recording paths both work from one capture).
- With System audio source = Browser, live mode behaves exactly as today (screen picker, ScriptProcessorNode tap for both sides).
- If the attach-capture frame names an unknown captureId, the panel shows a warning and continues as mic-only; the mic recording is never lost.
- Closing the live panel or the WebSocket mid-recording does not stop or corrupt the server capture; POST /api/capture/stop still returns a valid WAV.
- Groq and local engines both work for the server-fed Them chunks; the engine fallback rules in liveTranscription.ts apply unchanged.
- Unit tests cover the attach-capture control frame parsing and the live-sink PCM chunking into the accumulator with a synthetic 16 kHz buffer.
- project-context/transcription/live-transcription and project-context/architecture READMEs document the server-fed live path.
important_constraints:
- Do not change the binary WebSocket audio frame format; the new control frame is a separate text/JSON message.
- Keep the loopbackOnly guard on all capture endpoints.
- The WAV file output of a live-attached capture must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in format to a non-live capture (16 kHz mono pcm_s16le) so offset alignment and retranscribe keep working.
